Performers
Columbia Broadcasting Symphony (orchestra), Howard Barlow (conductor), Mitch Miller (oboe solo in the Intermezzo) Documented

The orchestra and conductor are credited by both sources. The oboe soloist is named only in the Archive item’s side list.

[1] [3]
Work version
Orchestral arrangement by Gordon Jacob of the military-band Folk Song Suite of 1923 Documented

The Archive description says this appears to be the only 78-rpm recording of the Jacob orchestration; the Discogs label credit names Jacob as arranger. The Burgess Hill programme note says Jacob made the transcription in 1924 but that it was not published until 1942, so how Barlow’s 1939 orchestra obtained the score is not established here.

[1] [3] [4]
Recorded
1939-12-19 Documented

Given in the Archive description as December 19, 1939.

[1]
Place
Unknown Unknown

Neither source names the studio or city.

[1] [3]
Label
Columbia Masterworks (United States); English Columbia (United Kingdom) Documented

Two ten-inch 78-rpm records in each issue.

[1] [3]
Catalogue
Set X-159 (17188-D, 17189-D), March 1940; later MX-159 (17234-D, 17235-D), 1941; English Columbia DB 1930–⁠1931, September 1940 Documented

The Archive description gives the American numbers and issue dates; Discogs catalogues the English pair DB 1930/1931 as 1940.

[1] [3]
Matrix, take, sides
Side 1 CO 25602-2 (first movement); side 2 CO 25603-1 and side 3 CO 25604-1 (Intermezzo, parts 1 and 2); side 4 CO 25605-1 (third movement) Documented

Stated in the Archive item’s description; the labels and stampers were not examined for this dossier.

[1]
Transfer
Internet Archive “Shellackophile” recordings collection Documented

The item is filed in that collection; no transfer engineer is named in the description.

[1]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

The Archive upload date (22 March 2022) is not a transfer date.

[1]
Processing
FLAC original with a variable-bitrate MP3 derivative, joined from four 78-rpm sides into one file. Documented

Equalisation, speed correction and noise reduction are not documented.

[1] [2]
Composition rights
Vaughan Williams’s copyright in the music runs to the end of 2028 in the UK and EU; Jacob’s arrangement has its own term. Documented

The Vaughan Williams Foundation gives 2028 as the year copyright in his music expires. IMSLP marks the suite as not in the public domain in the EU. Composition and arrangement rights are separate from the recording.

[6] [5]
Recording rights
Territorial EU phonogram public-domain basis: commercial issue in 1940, before 1963 Inferred, not documented

The project’s eu-published-before-1963 rule applies to the English Columbia issue of 1940 and the American set of March 1940: the former 50-year phonogram term had expired before the 2013 extension. This is not United States or worldwide clearance and not a Creative Commons licence.

[1] [3] [7]

Ralph Vaughan Williams, English Folk Song Suite (arranged by Gordon Jacob); Columbia Broadcasting Symphony, Howard Barlow. Columbia Masterworks X-159 (1940) and English Columbia DB 1930–⁠1931 (1940), Internet Archive transfer. Territorial EU phonogram basis only; the composition and arrangement remain in copyright.
